purpose: Bounded Fair Work Commission case preserving an unfair-dismissal finding, medical and workplace-access constraint, reported back-pay payment, continuity order, and failure of actual return while a risk assessment was used.

events.geography: South Australia; Fair Work Commission Sportsmed SA appeal [2015] FWCFB 1523
events.date_precision: back-pay and continuity implementation reported on 14 August 2014; Full Bench decision dated 27 February 2015
events.denominator: One publicly adjudicated worker case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission Full Bench decision [2015] FWCFB 1523
events.missingness: Private medical, payroll, household, treatment, alternative-job, and later-employment records are not retained; exact net payment, later remedy execution, final employment outcome, and post-decision livelihood are not observed
events.exposure: The worker suffered a non-work-related motor-vehicle injury, returned with restrictions, stopped working, and was terminated from her CSSD Manager role on 7 November 2013; the Commission found the dismissal unfair
events.alternatives_before_action: The public record does not identify a completed alternative job, accessible redeployment, household buffer, or feasible substitute income
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: A remedy order restored lost pay and continuity, but the employer did not permit actual return while a medical/risk assessment was undertaken; the worker was treated as on unpaid leave
events.choice_or_response: The worker pursued the unfair-dismissal route, attended the workplace and risk assessment, appealed the conditional reinstatement, and sought a real return rather than only contractual restoration
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The employer controlled workplace access and risk-assessment implementation; medical assessors supplied capacity evidence; the worker controlled appeal participation; the Commission controlled the remedy and legal interpretation
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The Commission ordered reinstatement, continuity, and restoration of lost pay; the record reports back pay paid on or about 14 August 2014. The Full Bench held that the conditional order did not achieve actual reinstatement, set it aside, and issued separate unconditional reinstatement order PR561823 requiring reinstatement within 14 days. A later Federal Circuit Court record reports that she returned on 26 March 2015 but disputed whether the materially altered role was genuine reinstatement
events.remedy_receipt: The decision reports that Sportsmed paid the back pay owing under the order and paid wages for a further two weeks, while actual work access was not restored; net amount and final payment status are not independently audited
events.durability_followup: The later court record observes a return on 26 March 2015, materially altered duties and status, cessation of work on 24 June 2015 while still employed, and an unresolved constructive-reinstatement dispute; later employment, household recovery, trust, and exit remain unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Lost pay and continuity were reported restored, but the worker did not return to the workplace and the conditional reinstatement was held unauthorized
events.protected_outcome: Money and legal continuity were protected to some extent; actual work access, role restoration, and durable livelihood were not protected in the observed period
events.sacrificed_outcome: The worker remained without actual work and was treated as on unpaid leave despite payment implementation; health, dignity, household, and future-career effects are not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The employer paid back wages but retained practical control over workplace entry through the risk-assessment process; the worker carried continued access and livelihood risk
events.later_outcome: The Full Bench replaced the conditional order with unconditional reinstatement order PR561823. The later court record reports actual return on 26 March 2015, disputed role degradation, and cessation of work on 24 June 2015 while still employed; no retained public record verifies final compensation, later employment, household recovery, trust, or exit
events.meaning_and_attribution: The decision makes practical restoration and workplace access legally distinct from payment and continuity; it does not provide a standardized worker trust or dignity measure
events.public_or_collective_response: Individual tribunal appeal and formal medical/risk-assessment process are observed; no later collective or political response is reported
events.counterexample: Back pay can be paid and continuity maintained while the person still cannot return to the job; money and access are separate remedy currencies
events.source_and_uncertainty: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2015] FWCFB 1523, https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/decisionssigned/html/2015fwcfb1523.htm, including separate reinstatement order PR561823; later Federal Circuit Court judgment [2015] FCCA 2140 is retained through a public case-text copy at https://www.casechat.au/cases/au/cartisano-v-sportsmed-sa-hospitals-pty-ltd and reports return, altered duties, cessation while still employed, and the unresolved constructive-reinstatement dispute. Neither record establishes final livelihood or household recovery

arrows.evidence: The decision records injury, restricted return, termination, an unfair-dismissal finding, and subsequent remedy proceedings
arrows.counterexample: An unfair-dismissal finding does not by itself establish medical recovery or a usable job alternative
arrows.remaining_gap: Health trajectory, household resources, redeployment, and substitute work

arrows.evidence: The decision reports back pay paid on or about 14 August 2014 and continuity maintained through that date
arrows.counterexample: Payment and continuity do not establish actual work or usable restoration
arrows.remaining_gap: Exact net payment, benefits, final payment, and adequacy

arrows.to: risk assessment and no actual return
arrows.evidence: The worker attended the workplace for assessment and was initially not permitted to return; after unconditional order PR561823, the later court record reports that she returned on 26 March 2015, then disputed materially altered duties and ceased work on 24 June 2015 while remaining employed
arrows.counterexample: A legal or payroll restoration can coexist with continued exclusion from the actual workplace
arrows.remaining_gap: Whether the altered role satisfied the reinstatement order, final remedy, later employment, and household recovery

arrows.to: Full Bench ruling that reinstatement must be real and practical
arrows.evidence: The Full Bench held that a condition allowing no actual return was beyond power and set aside the order for rehearing
arrows.counterexample: A stronger legal standard does not show the individual ultimately returned or recovered
arrows.remaining_gap: Compliance with unconditional order, later employment, alternative compensation, and later livelihood

arrows.to: durable livelihood, trust, recovery, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public record closes at payment, no return, unpaid-leave treatment, and legal correction of the conditional remedy
arrows.counterexample: Money can be delivered while role access and future security remain unresolved
arrows.remaining_gap: Final remedy, later work after June 2015, household security, health, trust, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger provides a strong same-case implementation boundary: reported back-pay payment and continuity coexist with no actual return, and the tribunal explicitly distinguishes legal payment from real and practical reinstatement. It does not establish final remedy, causality of non-return, or later recovery.
storage_boundary: No private medical, payroll, household, or employment file is retained; only bounded public decision fields, dates, remedy terms, implementation, non-return, uncertainty, and open downstream arrows are represented.
